correctness.rationale: Substitution into the source formulas gives duplicated \(D_x\) Wootters weights and hence \(C_x=0\) for every positive temperature. The \(D_y\) formula reduces to a single exponential-polynomial numerator. After positive rescaling its derivative is strictly positive, proving one and only one threshold. The bundled verifier independently replays the formulas and numerical bracket; finite numerics are not used for the continuum proof.

originality.rationale: The 2009 source contains the general concurrence formulas and the pairwise directional dominance assertion, but does not identify their incompatibility. The accepted statement is the explicit exact counterexample family and its unique temperature threshold. The 2019 full treatment analyzes mixed-sign/nonmonotone single-axis thresholds and cites the 2009 paper, but the inspected text does not state or repair the pairwise \(D_x\)-versus-\(D_y\) ordering. Focused published-finding and web searches located no prior statement of this correction. Residual risk is retained because the family is derivable by specialization of known formulas.
residual_risks: The exact family is a specialization of already-published concurrence formulas; originality is specifically the correction to the published directional-ordering assertion and the threshold mechanism.
A later paper not surfaced by the focused searches may have independently noted the same inconsistency.

value.rationale: The result corrects a published qualitative design rule rather than adding an arbitrary parameter point. It isolates the missing third-coupling dependence: a symmetry-induced level degeneracy can completely extinguish thermal concurrence for one DM direction while the competing direction remains entangled on an exact interval. This gives a concrete boundary condition for directional-DM control claims.
